title: On-call and incident response playbook — comprehensive
author: Avery Chen
summary: Company-wide playbook covering incident lifecycle, runbook conventions, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations and handoffs, game-day guidance, and customer/status-page communication templates.
body:
Purpose

This document defines Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response practices. It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and product owners who will act as responders, incident commanders (ICs), or stakeholders during service-impacting events. The playbook codifies: incident lifecycle and severity matrix, runbook formatting and examples, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation rules and handoffs, regular game days, and templates for status page and customer communications.

Scope

- Applies to all production services that impact customer-facing inference (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane).
- Includes service-level incidents (availability, data integrity, severe performance regressions) and security incidents that require immediate engineering response.
- Excludes routine customer tickets and feature bug fixes unless escalated by support or product into an incident.

Definitions

- Incident: An event that results in service degradation or disruption affecting customer experience, billing, or security.
- Incident Commander (IC): Single point of coordination during an active incident. Responsible for triage, escalation, and communications.
- Responder: Engineer actively executing runbooks or mitigation steps.
- Major Incident: Severity 1 incident per the severity matrix below. Triggers page to executive stakeholders and status page update.
- Postmortem: A blameless writeup after mitigations are complete explaining root cause, impact, timeline, and corrective actions.

Roles and Responsibilities

- On-call Engineer (Primary): First responder. Triage, run immediate checks, attempt mitigation.
- Secondary/Backup: Help with remediation and act as escalation path if Primary needs offload.
- Incident Commander (IC): Takes over coordination if incident meets Major criteria or after first 30 minutes if unclear.
- Engineering Manager: Decision authority for paging additional teams, approving customer credits.
- Product Owner / Customer Success: Liaison for customer-facing communications and prioritization.
- Security: Engaged immediately for incidents involving data exposure or suspected compromise.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)

1) Detection and Triage
  - Alert triggers via PagerDuty/Sentry/Prometheus.
  - Primary on-call acknowledges within 5 minutes.
  - Run initial triage checklist in the runbook: confirm alert validity, check upstream/downstream dependencies, gather recent deploys.

2) Classify Severity and Escalate
  - Use the Severity Matrix below to classify. For Severity 1, IC is declared and execs + CS are notified.

3) Mitigate and Contain
  - Follow the appropriate runbook (service-specific). Typical steps: failover, scale-up, cache clear, rollback, or traffic routing to fallback model variant.

4) Communicate
  - Internal: Update #incidents Slack channel with status headers every 15 minutes.
  - External: Update status page (see templates) for S1/S2. Customer Success drafts targeted customer emails if needed.

5) Resolve and Verify
  - Confirm system health for 30 minutes post-mitigation and monitor for recurrence.

6) Postmortem and Remediation
  - Create postmortem within 72 hours (initial draft) and finalize within 10 business days. Include RCA, timeline, impact, mitigations, and action owners.

Severity matrix (use for classification)

| Severity | Definition | Typical impact | Paging/Comms | Target MTTR |
|----------|------------|----------------|--------------|-------------|
| S1 (Major) | Complete or near-complete outage impacting many customers (production API unavailable, control plane down, critical security incident) | All customers or large fraction, revenue and SLA impact | Page on-call immediately, declare IC, exec + CS notified, update status page | 1-4 hours (aim for <1 hour for partial mitigation) |
| S2 | Significant degradation of service (high error rates, high tail latency, partial region impact) | Multiple customers affected, degraded UX | Page on-call, escalate to IC if not resolved within 30-60 minutes, update status page | 4-24 hours |
| S3 | Limited impact (single customer, minor feature regression) | Few customers affected, workarounds exist | Create incident ticket, notify stakeholders, no immediate page typically | 24-72 hours |
| S4 | Informational / scheduled maintenance | Planned work or low-risk issues | No paging; communicate via scheduled status updates | N/A |

Escalation matrix (quick view)

- Primary on-call -> Secondary -> Service Owner -> IC -> Engineering Manager -> CTO

On-call rotations and handoffs

- Rotation cadence: weekly primary rotations (Mon 00:00 UTC to next Mon 00:00 UTC) with a secondary on-call paired to the primary.
- Paging policy: Primary must acknowledge PagerDuty within 5 minutes and update incident channel within 10 minutes.
- Handoff checklist (required for every rotation):
  1. New primary confirms calendar and PagerDuty contact.
  2. Review active incidents and current mitigations.
  3. Export last 24h alerts and outstanding Jira incident tasks.
  4. Update on-call notes in the team wiki (two-line summary).
  5. Confirm Slack DND and escalation overrides.

Runbook conventions and authoring standards

- Runbooks live alongside service documentation under confluence eng-team wikis and must follow this format:
  - Title, Purpose, Owner, PagerDuty escalation key, Preconditions, Quick checks, Mitigation steps (ordered, numbered), Verification steps, Rollback steps, Post-incident actions.
- Keep runbooks short and prescriptive with exact commands and dashboards referenced.
- Include CLI snippets, terraform/apply safety notes, and required approvals for destructive actions.
- Versioning: Append date and author to runbook header and maintain changelog.

Runbook examples (embedded)

1) High-tail-latency (inference API) — quick triage
  - Purpose: Bring tail latency below SLA when p95/p99 > target.
  - Owner: inference-runtime-team oncall
  - Quick checks:
    a) Check recent deploys: "git log --since='2 hours' --pretty=oneline" on api repo.
    b) Grafana: query "service_inference_latency_p99" for affected regions.
    c) Check autoscaler and GPU pool: "kubectl get hpa,deploy -n inference" and "kubectl describe node <gpu-node>".
  - Mitigation (ordered):
    1. Enable emergency burst capacity for Dedicated customers (console toggle) or scale up GPU pool by +20% (ops runbook).
    2. Temporarily route non-critical traffic to cheaper model variants or cached responses.
    3. If recent deploy suspected, rollback to previous stable revision: "kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-api -n prod --to-revision=<rev>".
  - Verification: p99 latency below SLO for 30 minutes, error rate <= baseline.

2) GPU OOM / worker crash — quick mitigation
  - Purpose: Restore worker pool health and prevent cascading failures.
  - Quick checks: "kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep OOM"; check kernel logs on node.
  - Mitigation:
    1. Mark node unschedulable: "kubectl cordon <node>" and drain: "kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data".
    2. Recreate worker pod with reduced batch size environment variable: BATCH_SIZE=1.
    3. If hardware fault suspected, escalate to infra (paging ops team).
  - Verification: worker pod restarts healthy and job queue drains; no further OOMs in 30 minutes.

Postmortem process and template

- Timelines: initial postmortem draft within 72 hours, final within 10 business days.
- Must be blameless and include: summary, impact (customers, API keys, regions), timeline (UTC timestamps), root cause analysis, contributing factors, resolution steps, action items with owners and due dates, follow-up validation plan.
- Severity 1 incidents require a postmortem readout in the engineering review meeting within two weeks.

Mandatory postmortem sections (use as headings in the postmortem page)

1. Title and incident ID
2. Summary (2-3 sentence customer-facing summary)
3. Impact (number of affected customers, duration, SLA/financial impact if known)
4. Timeline (chronological list of events with UTC timestamps)
5. Root cause analysis (single root cause + evidence)
6. Contributing factors
7. Mitigation and recovery steps taken
8. Corrective actions and owners (with due dates)
9. Post-incident validation plan
10. Lessons learned and follow-ups

Game days and reliability exercises

- Cadence: quarterly team-level game days; company-wide simulated major incident exercise annually.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, exercise on-call rotations, test fallbacks (model variant routing, cache restores), and practice customer comms.
- Example exercise: Simulated region outage where primary model variant fails and traffic must be routed to quantized fallback with a 10% quantization-induced quality regression tolerated.
- Post-game-day deliverables: annotated runbook changes, action owners, improvement backlog items.

Status page and customer communications templates

- Status page is the canonical external source (status.redwoodinference.com). For S1/S2 incidents, update immediately with a concise summary and expected next update time.
- Use the following templates when posting updates: copy/paste and edit.

Incident start (status page / customer-facing):
Title: Degraded inference performance in <region> / Partial outage\Description: We are investigating reports of increased latency and errors for the Redwood Inference API in <region>. Our on-call team is actively triaging. We will provide an update by <time in UTC, e.g., in 15 minutes>. Impact: Some requests may return errors or experience delayed responses. Workaround: Consider routing traffic to another region or model variant if available.

Customer update (email / targeted):
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood Inference in <region> — current status\Hi <Customer name>,
We are currently investigating an issue affecting the Redwood Inference API in <region> that may cause increased latency or errors for inference requests. Our on-call and SRE teams are actively working to identify root cause and restore full service. We will follow up with updates every 30 minutes or as significant progress is made.
If you'd like us to route your traffic to a different region or model variant while we restore service, please reply and include your account ID.
Thanks for your patience,
<Incident Commander name>

Incident resolved (status page / customer-facing):
Title: Service restored — Redwood Inference in <region>\Description: The issue impacting the Redwood Inference API in <region> has been resolved. Normal service has been restored and verified. We are preparing a postmortem with details and will share it within 10 business days. Impact: <concise summary>.

Internal incident update cadence and channel usage

- Slack: #incidents for live updates; #oncall-summaries for post-incident synopses.
- PagerDuty: primary paging and escalation.
- Incident document: create Jira incident ticket with ID and link in Slack header.
- Update cadence: every 15 minutes for S1 incidents, every 30 minutes for S2 until mitigation in place.

Metrics, SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)

- Inference API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for hosted API (global). Alert thresholds: availability <99.9% over 10 minutes triggers S1 investigation.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms, p99 < 1s for standard models. Alert: p99 > 1.2s sustained for 5 minutes -> S2.
- Error budget policy: If monthly error budget consumption exceeds 80%, escalate to reliability review and freeze non-critical deploys.

Tools and integrations

- PagerDuty: primary paging rules and escalation policies.
- Grafana/Prometheus: primary monitoring and dashboards.
- Sentry: application error aggregation and stack traces.
- Confluence: canonical runbooks and postmortems.
- Jira: incident tickets and action items.

Operational runbook maintenance

- Each service owner must review runbooks quarterly and after any incident.
- Runbook changes require an owner, date, and short rationale entry in the runbook changelog.

Related pages and references

- eng-sre/capacity-planning (link internal)
- eng-infra/runbooks (link internal)
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture (link internal)

Appendix: Quick reference snippets

- Acknowledge PagerDuty on-call: "pd acknowledge <incident-id>" (CLI)
- Create incident Jira: template project INCDNT -> include tags: severity, services, incident-owner
- Quick Grafana queries: "sum(rate(http_request_errors_total[5m])) by (service)", "histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))"

Contact and ownership

- On-call owner (process): eng-sre team
- Playbook owner: Avery Chen (eng-sre)
- Postmortem owner: incident commander for the incident

Document maintenance

- This playbook is reviewed quarterly by eng-sre and updated after each major incident or game-day.
